what_its_for: Dapagliflozin is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is also used to reduce the risk of hospitalization or death in adults with heart failure, and to slow the progression of chronic kidney disease in adults who are at risk of kidney damage getting worse.
how_to_take: Take dapagliflozin by mouth with or without food, usually once a day in the morning. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Drink plenty of fluids throughout the day to stay well hydrated unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg once daily in the morning. Your doctor may increase your dose to 10 mg once daily if needed and if your body tolerates the lower dose well. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different based on your condition and kidney function.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store dapagliflozin at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it in the original container, away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not store in the bathroom. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely through a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid becoming dehydrated — drink enough fluids daily, especially in hot weather or when exercising. Avoid drinking excessive amounts of alcohol, as it can affect your blood sugar and increase the risk of a rare but serious condition called diabetic ketoacidosis. Avoid activities that may cause genital or urinary tract infections, and practice good hygiene in the genital area. Talk to your doctor before taking over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen or naproxen, as they can affect kidney function.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, or confusion (signs of diabetic ketoacidosis); signs of a urinary tract infection such as burning when you urinate, frequent urination, or pain in your lower back or pelvis; pain, redness, swelling, or tenderness in the genital or anal area (a rare but serious infection called Fournier's gangrene); signs of low blood sugar such as shakiness, sweating, dizziness, or confusion; signs of dehydration such as dizziness, lightheadedness, or feeling faint; decreased urination or swelling in your legs or feet (possible kidney problems); or any allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Dapagliflozin starts working within a few days of starting treatment, but it may take several weeks to see the full benefit on your blood sugar levels. For heart failure and kidney disease, the protective effects build up over weeks to months. Continue taking this medication even if you feel well, as it works best when taken consistently every day.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): You may be at a higher risk of dehydration and dizziness. Make sure to drink enough fluids and rise slowly from sitting or lying positions. Kidney problems: This medication may not work as well if your kidney function is reduced. Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. Pregnancy: Do NOT take dapagliflozin during the second or third trimester of pregnancy, as it may harm the unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if dapagliflozin passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medication. Children: Dapagliflozin is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age for most conditions. Ask your doctor if it is appropriate for your child.
